step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified client ingest sources from the diagram and transcript: Focus Camera (UserConsumerCamera), Mobile App (UserConsumerMobile), and Web Platform (UserConsumerWeb).
2. Identified storage and queuing layer: S3 bucket for video storage and SQS for job queueing.
3. Identified target tracking auto-scaling control loop: CloudWatch metrics queried by a custom Lambda function to calculate message-to-instance ratios, which then instructs the Spot Fleet (AutoScaling) group.
4. Identified compute layer: EC2 worker instances pulled jobs from SQS, transcoded videos, and wrote playable video back to S3.
5. Categorized edges into three distinct flows: Flow 0 for video upload & job queuing, Flow 1 for auto-scaling management, and Flow 2 for transcoding execution and playable video output storage.

graph.name: Hudl Sports Video Transcoding Architecture
graph.notes: Hudl ingests coaching videos via mobile, web, and hardware camera apps into S3 while sending messages to prioritized SQS queues. A custom Lambda scaling function queries CloudWatch metrics to dynamically adjust a Spot Fleet Auto Scaling group. EC2 worker instances transcode jobs from SQS and save the output back to S3 within 2 minutes.

nodes.name: Focus Camera
nodes.notes: Dedicated Hudl Focus hardware camera for automated video capture.

nodes.name: Mobile App
nodes.notes: Mobile app client used by coaches to upload video content.

nodes.name: Web Platform
nodes.notes: Web interface client used to upload videos and trigger job queues.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores raw video uploads and transcoded playable video output within 2 minutes.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Multiple prioritized message queues handling up to 30,000 messages/minute based on user priority and job size.

nodes.name: CloudWatch
nodes.notes: Collects queue depth metrics used by Lambda for target tracking.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Evaluates SQS queue depth versus instance count and calculates target tracking ratio to trigger auto-scaling.

nodes.name: Spot Fleet
nodes.notes: Manages over 20 instance types across Spot Fleet, scaling up to 10,000+ instances during peak game nights.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Worker compute instances that process video transcoding tasks, reducing total compute costs by 28%.

edges.notes: Mobile app uploads raw coaching video directly to S3.
Web platform uploads raw coaching video directly to S3.
Focus camera uploads raw video directly to S3.
Initiates upload and sends transcoding job message to prioritized SQS queue.
SQS queue depth is monitored to determine pending job count.
CloudWatch metrics are queried by Lambda to calculate ratio of messages to instances.
Lambda invokes Spot Fleet Auto Scaling Group to scale instances in or out based on load ratio.
EC2 worker instances pull queued transcoding messages from SQS.
Transcoded video is written back into S3 bucket in playable format.
